title: Fallout Docket — Weekly SRE Sync (Nov 07 2029)
content:
Purpose:
A condensed, action-oriented weekly sync for SRE focused on the small outage windows we saw Tuesday–Thursday this week plus the on-call handoff notes for next rotation. This is intentionally terse — use linked artifacts for deep dive traces and the postmortem draft.

TL;DR:
- Multiple short-duration errors (5–90s) across hosted inference in us-west-2 caused transient SLO pressure; root cause appears to be autoscaler metric oscillation + unexpected KV cache invalidation after a kernel update.
- Current SLO status: availability for text-generation route = 99.85% (rolling 7d), target = 99.9% -> error budget ~0.05% remaining. Latency P95 breached twice (700ms) during spikes.
- Immediate mitigations applied: manual scale-up + pinned model variant (v1.8-stable) to force local cache warm state; autoscaler metric smoothing reverted to previous config.
- Owners assigned for follow-ups: autoscaler tuning (Jonas), KV cache regression triage (María), runbook augment + synthetic test (Aisha).

Incident timeline (summary):
- 2029-11-05 02:42 UTC — first spike, repeated 5–30s errors on /v1/generate; on-call (Samir) triaged, suspected gateway flaps; applied temporary routing to standby pool.
- 2029-11-06 14:10 UTC — larger event after kernel-level model runtime (small patch) rolled to canary; KV cache invalidation triggered cold starts and a flurry of traffic -> local batching backpressure; autoscaler started oscillating due to burst_metric smoothing set to 0.
- 2029-11-06 14:25 UTC — manual intervention: revert runtime patch on canary, pin model variant, force instance warm pools. Latency normalized by 14:48 UTC.
- 2029-11-07 09:03 UTC — Post-action verification run and synthetic traffic showed restored behavior; but 7d rolling SLO still flagged.

Key observations + hypotheses (notes-to-self style):
- Autoscaler: oscillation caused by metric smoothing = 0 (new default from tooling change). Short bursts create oscillating scale events; need hysteresis and minimum stable window.
- KV cache: the runtime patch introduced a race where cache invalidation propagated to nodes in the wrong order; causes wide cold-cache fanout; root cause likely an ordering bug in the invalidation message handler.
- Batching/backpressure: when many cold starts occur, the continuous-batcher queues blow up and trigger upstream timeouts from API gateway; TTLs and queue-size protections need revisiting.

Metrics snapshot (rolling 7d window at time of last_modified):
- Text-generation availability: 99.85% (target 99.9%)
- Error budget consumed: ~50% of weekly budget (we consumed ~0.05% of total tokens)
- P95 latency: baseline 220ms, spikes up to 720ms during cold-start surge
- Autoscale events: 24 scale activities in 6 hours during peak (normal: ~3–6)

Action items (owner — ETA) [prioritized]:
1) Autoscaler smoothing & hysteresis change: Jonas — short-term patch to restore previous smoothing value + add a 60s stable window for scale-down. ETA: 2029-11-12.
2) KV cache invalidation regression: María — reproduce locally with instrumentation, add ordering guard, write unit tests. ETA: 2029-11-15.
3) Runbook: Aisha — add a dedicated 'cold-cache surge' checklist (quick pin variant, manual warm, route to standby pool). Include clear escalation steps and metrics to watch (queue depth, cold-start rate). ETA: 2029-11-10.
4) Synthetic test: Samir — add a nightly EWMA-based cold-start synthetic that injects cache invalidation and measures downstream P95 and queue depth. ETA: 2029-11-13.
5) Capacity check: infra (cc: platform-eng) — confirm standby pool sizing for us-west-2 and add automated alarms when standing pool falls below 3 nodes. ETA: 2029-11-14.
6) Postmortem draft: Aisha/Jonas — first pass with RCA, timeline, and RCA verification plan. ETA: 2029-11-11.

On-call handoff notes (next rotation: 2029-11-10 to 2029-11-17):
- Primary: Jonas Kim (pagerduty schedule updated)
- Secondary: María Alvarez
- Critical runbooks: linked in Confluence (OPS-4567-autoscaler-postmortem) and local runbook entry 'cold-cache-surge' (WIP)
- Immediate watch thresholds to escalate:
  - http 5xx > 0.5% for 5m on /v1/generate -> escalate to on-call + platform-eng
  - cold-start rate > 3% over 10m -> escalate to eng-sre (page primary)
  - autoscaler > 6 scale operations in 15m -> page on-call and notify infra
- Testing note: if you observe oscillation, DO NOT trigger a global scale down; set to manual and contact Jonas.

Follow-up meeting slots (calendar invites sent):
- Monday 2029-11-11 15:00 UTC — RCA walkthrough (Aisha leads)
- Wednesday 2029-11-13 08:00 UTC — Autoscaler config review (Jonas + infra)
- Friday 2029-11-15 17:00 UTC — Runbook signoff (Aisha + Samir + María)

Open questions / unresolved items (for action during RCA):
- Did the runtime patch change any message format that could affect ordering semantics? (runtime-eng answer pending)
- Do we need a new metric for 'cache-invalidation-fanout' to trigger earlier detection?
- Should we introduce a small randomized jitter in invalidation propagation to reduce simultaneous cold starts?

Notes / raw scraps from triage (copied from pager thread):
- "observed massive simultaneous cold starts, queue depth spiked to 12k and gateway started 502ing" — Samir
- "autoscaler smoothing default changed in toolchain PR #1189, I reverted locally and spikes subsided" — Jonas
- "we should add a test that simulates invalidation order inversion" — María

Attachments & artifacts to review: see linked_artifacts above. In addition, check the trace dump at: https://traces.redwood.company/trace/2029-11-06-coldstart-fanout (internal)

Quick retrospective notes:
- Good: rapid detection via synthetic-sweep, clear manual runbook steps helped contain blast radius.
- Improve: we lacked a focused synthetic test for invalidation order; autoscaler defaults got drifted by a toolchain change and landed without a gate.

If you are reading this and are assigned an action, please add progress updates inline in the doc or reply in the incident Slack thread (channel #sre-ops). If you need more context ping me @aisha.

-- Aisha

(rough brainstorm: consider a small 'graceful-warm' handoff where new instances announce warm-readiness to a coordination topic before taking traffic — design sketch in Confluence link above)
